claim.why_it_matters: The PDF prints 4.3 as a numbered subsection heading, the same style as 4.1 and 4.2 on page 722, which the markdown renders as '### 4.1 ...' and '### 4.2 ...'; here it is a plain paragraph (as are the errata-inserted 4.4 and 4.5 headings on the same page), so the subsection is invisible to heading-based navigation (informative History of COBOL appendix).

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page 723 (300 dpi) prints '4.3 ISO STANDARD 1989-1985 FOR COBOL' on its own line above the body text, as a numbered subsection heading. In page-722.md, 4.1 (line 7) and 4.2 (line 15) are marked '### 4.1 ...' and '### 4.2 ...'. In page-723.md, '4.3 ISO STANDARD 1989-1985 FOR COBOL' is a plain paragraph, and so are the errata-inserted '4.4 ISO 1989:1985/Amd.1:1992' and '4.5 ISO 1989:1985/Amd.2:1994'. The heading text matches word for word, so no content is missing. The defect is heading markup: the transcription marks sibling subsections inconsistently, so 4.3 through 4.5 do not appear in heading-based navigation. The section is informative (History of COBOL), so the defect is structural and not normative.
verdict.corrected_description: No text is missing. The transcription leaves the subsection headings 4.3, 4.4 and 4.5 on page 723 as plain paragraphs, while 4.1 and 4.2 on page 722 are '###' headings. They should be '### 4.3 ISO STANDARD 1989-1985 FOR COBOL', with the errata-corrected 4.4 and 4.5 at the same level. This is informative, structural markup only.
